paper.title: Fortran 77 subroutines for computing the eigenvalues of Hamiltonian matrices II (HAPACK, Algorithm 854)

code.note: Fortran 77 HAPACK release 1.1 (03-Sep-2005) in Fortran77/Dp; the driver tdhaesu.f reads dhaesu.dat and prints the results that are shipped as dhaesu.res. Needs LAPACK and BLAS.

claim.location: Shipped reference file Fortran77/Dp/Drivers/dhaesu.res, section 'The stable eigenvalues', row i=1: WR(1) = -3.1941, WI(1) = 0.0000. Produced by tdhaesu.f from the input dhaesu.dat (N=5, balancing and job flags in the file). The paper's own table could not be read (ACM returns 403), so the paper location is not verified.
claim.value: -3.1941 (real part of the first stable eigenvalue of the DHAESU example)
claim.metric: real part WR(1) of the first stable eigenvalue, as printed to 4 decimals
claim.tolerance_reason: The reference is printed to 4 decimals, so the rounding half-unit is 5e-5; 1e-4 allows rounding of the last digit and nothing looser, and a different LAPACK or BLAS changes results far less than that.

cost.data_licence: ACM TOMS software distributed via netlib; the archive's own terms were not read in full

why: A deterministic eigenvalue of a fixed example matrix, computed by the Fortran code's own driver and recorded in a shipped reference file, so the method must run to reproduce it.
